Question Choices: What is the sum of the interior angle measures of any triangle? Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Hints: Draw a line parallel to one side through the opposite vertex.|The three angles form a straight angle.
Solution: Draw through one vertex a line parallel to the opposite side. Alternate interior angles place copies of the other two triangle angles beside the angle at that vertex, forming a straight angle. Their sum is 180 degrees.

Question Choices: A triangle has angles 35 degrees and 84 degrees. Find the third angle. Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Hints: Subtract the two known angles from 180 degrees.|35 + 84 = 119.
Solution: Triangle interior angles sum to 180 degrees. The known angles total 35 + 84 = 119, leaving 180 - 119 = 61 degrees.

Question Choices: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 40 degrees. Find each base angle. Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Hints: The base angles are congruent.|The two base angles share 180 - 40 degrees equally.
Solution: The base angles opposite the equal sides are equal. Together they measure 180 - 40 = 140 degrees, so each is 140/2 = 70 degrees.

Question Choices: An isosceles triangle has a base angle of 58 degrees. Find the vertex angle. Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Hints: Both base angles measure 58 degrees.|Subtract 2(58) from 180.
Solution: Both base angles measure 58 degrees. Their total is 116, leaving vertex angle 180 - 116 = 64 degrees.

Solution: By the isosceles triangle theorem, angles opposite two congruent sides are congruent. The equal side pair therefore gives an equal opposite angle pair.

Solution: By the converse of the isosceles triangle theorem, sides opposite two congruent angles are congruent. The equal angle pair therefore gives an equal opposite side pair.

Question Choices: What is the measure of each angle in an equilateral triangle? Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Hints: All three angles are congruent.|Divide the triangle angle sum by 3.
Solution: All three sides are equal, so all three opposite angles are equal. Their total is 180 degrees; each measures 180/3 = 60 degrees.

Question Choices: A triangle has exterior angle 125 degrees and one remote interior angle 52 degrees. Find the other remote interior angle. Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Hints: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.|Solve 52 + x = 125.
Solution: The exterior angle equals the sum of the remote interior angles: 125 = 52 + x. Subtract 52 to get x = 73 degrees.

Question Choices: In an isosceles triangle the vertex angle is twice each base angle. Find one base angle. Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Hints: Let each base angle be x.|Solve x + x + 2x = 180.
Solution: Let each equal base angle be x degrees. The vertex angle is 2x. Then x + x + 2x = 180, so 4x = 180 and x = 45 degrees. The angles 45, 45 and 90 total 180.
